S2 T3 morose-selfaware-unicorn: review-plan initially BLOCKED - a fourth aspirational claim. The plan credited the new operation (and the 'legacy sequence') with 'save' and 'dirty-gating' behavior, but apply_handlers._observe_rich_reemit NEVER calls save() - verified by reading it and grepping the function body for save(), which returns zero - it mutates the live entry in place and relies on the pass's later save, and BindingStore.save() is explicitly unconditional with no write elision. Remediated: corrected the AC from 'Unchanged data performs no save' to 'the operation performs NO save of its own on ANY path', changed the byte-parity AC to compare after ONE save rather than per emit, and recorded the correction. Re-review PASS signed. That is now four documented behaviors this epic found the code never implemented (double-bind safety-abort, alert dedup via timestamp_ns, comment-map never-remapped, and now per-emit save/dirty-gating).
IMPLEMENTED and PUSHED: Gerrit 1899. binding_lifecycle.py 533 LOC, binding_store.py 561. All 5 held-out discriminators passed unseen; 29/29 green; 3310 passed + 9 skipped; lint 0, typecheck 566, comment-hygiene 0 (the new lesson applied - I ran that gate and its guard test BEFORE pushing this time), config-ownership 0, module-size contract pass. Implementer: 1 attempt, and it correctly reported make lint red on MY visible-subset scaffold (an unused pytest alias and a missing blank line) rather than on its own code, proving the cause by stashing - the restored full oracle uses that alias and formats clean.
MUTATION FOUND ANOTHER REAL ORACLE GAP, third in the epic and the same shape as the others - the spy was too narrow. My no-save test patched only BindingStore.save, but the policy owner holds the repository DIRECTLY, so a self._repo.save() slipped into the operation never touches the facade method and the test stayed GREEN. Rewritten to count saves at BOTH layers; a repository-level per-emit save now drives it RED, verified. Also verified returning 0 instead of None for a missing binding drives the suite RED.
Verified -1 on patch set 1 root-caused immediately: docs/env-vars.md stale again, because adding note_rich_emit shifted the non-literal os.environ.get reference in binding_lifecycle.py from line 69 to 70. Regenerated and amended with the Change-Id preserved (patch set 2). This is the second time this generated file has gone stale from a line shift in this epic; ADR 0099 section 9 already documents the hazard, and it is now clear that ANY edit to a module containing a non-literal env read requires gen_env_registry.py before pushing.
